text:
support-alex: FYI — we started getting a small flood of p95/p99 latency complaints 6m after the runtime v7.3.0 canary rolled at ~09:12 PDT. Multiple customers on hosted API: increased tail latency and some timeouts. I grabbed a few request IDs: req_3f7a, req_3f9b, req_401c. Dashboard shows p95 ~2.1s -> 6.3s, p99 ~3.4s -> 12.8s.

deploy-bot: [automated] canary: runtime:v7.3.0 deployed to canary pool (3/50 nodes) at 2026-03-15T09:12:04Z by @zoe-eng :rocket:

maria-runtime: thanks Alex. Any repro curl or model skew info? which models and seq lengths affected?

support-alex: most reports for text-generation v2 endpoints using open-llama-13b and our rdalpha-7b variant; seq lengths vary but many >512; happens for streaming and non-streaming. I can repro locally with a replay from prod trace — see sample curl below.

support-alex: ```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"open-llama-13b","input":"<500 tokens prompt>"}'
```

eli-oncall: pinging oncall. I just checked the latency heatmap — spike aligns exactly with canary push window. Looks like p95 jump localized to canary nodes. Need to triage quickly but hold off wide rollout.

raj-sre: looking at infra metrics now. Not seeing GPU saturation or OOMs. CPU on host is normal. However there is a sharp increase in RPC retries between frontend and runtime shards for canary nodes. Traces show extra 150-200ms spent in internal RPC per token for affected requests.

zoe-eng: that's interesting — v7.3.0 included two runtime changes: 1) new attention kernel switch for long sequences (commit 5d2b9c) and 2) an aggressive KV-cache prefetch / eviction tweak (commit 7a1f00). Both were behind canary toggle but default enabled in this roll.

maria-runtime: can we toggle those features back on canary nodes independently? If RPC retries are up, could be backpressure from the kernel change causing slower per-step times and retries in the async pipeline.

raj-sre: I can query traces for internal RPC error codes. Quick check: increased 503/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED headers between workers on canary. Might be transient backpressure.

eli-oncall: action plan: 1) Flip the prefetch/eviction toggle off on canary nodes, 2) if no improvement in 10m, rollback canary v7.3.0.

zoe-eng: flipping toggle now on canary pool: `rv runtime toggle --pool canary --flag kv_prefetch=false --commit 7a1f00`

deploy-bot: [automated] feature-toggle: kv_prefetch set to false on canary pool by @zoe-eng at 2026-03-15T09:24:31Z

maria-runtime: after toggle, I'm seeing p95 drop from ~6.2s to ~2.4s within two minutes for a subset of requests. p99 still a bit high but trending down.

support-alex: customers confirming latencies improving for those who reported. One customer still seeing 8-9s tail — sharing their req id to triage: req_410d.

raj-sre: diving into req_410d trace — that one hit a canary node that still had older prefetch logic? Hmm shows a mix of canary variants; maybe some requests routed to different canary instances. I'll run a targeted grep on the router logs to see which instance served the request.

raj-sre: found it — instance canary-7 returned by router had the kernel switch still enabled (5d2b9c). So we have two independent flags: kv_prefetch and new_attention_kernel. We only toggled prefetch.

eli-oncall: we need to decide: toggle kernel back OR rollback canary. Given the kernel affects inner loop, it might be the main suspect for persistent p99. Any data on per-token latency delta from the kernel?

zoe-eng: I ran microbenchmarks before rollout: for short sequences the kernel was faster, for sequences >1024 it regressed because of additional memory copies. Our canary set had a handful of high-seq customers; we missed that in canary sampling. Commit: 5d2b9c. Suggest toggling kernel off on canary first.

maria-runtime: toggle command: `rv runtime toggle --pool canary --flag new_attention_kernel=false --commit 5d2b9c`

deploy-bot: [automated] feature-toggle: new_attention_kernel set to false on canary pool by @maria-runtime at 2026-03-15T09:38:12Z

raj-sre: after kernel toggle, internal RPC retries evaporated in traces. p95 now 1.8s, p99 2.9s — back near baseline. Marking immediate incident mitigation success.

eli-oncall: good. Rolling back rollout to pause further progression of v7.3.0 while we bisect commits. Action: set rollout paused and revert canary->stable promotion.

zoe-eng: `rv deploy pause --rollout runtime:v7.3.0` and schedule a canary-rollback job to clear instances serving with flags still on.

deploy-bot: [automated] rollout: runtime:v7.3.0 promotion paused by @eli-oncall at 2026-03-15T09:45:00Z

maria-runtime: initial bisect notes: likely culprits are 5d2b9c (attention kernel) and 7a1f00 (kv prefetch). Both contributed but kernel was dominant for long sequences. We'll create a bisect job that deploys a variant with only one change at a time across a small canary subset.

raj-sre: I'll run targeted A/B traces to compare per-token micro-latency and RPC counts. Also adding a temporary alert for internal RPC retries > 50/min on any pool.

support-alex: customers are satisfied with interim fixes, thanks. Will communicate status: mitigated by toggles, rollout paused, working on root cause and permanent fix.

zoe-eng: follow-up tasks (assigned):
- revert attention kernel code path and rework memory copy strategy (owner: zoe-eng)
- harden canary sampling to include >512/1024 seq workloads (owner: maria-runtime)
- add perf regression checks to PRs touching kernels (owner: eng-ml)
- update runbook: when seeing p95 jump within canary window, check kernel flags + kv_prefetch first (owner: eli-oncall)

eli-oncall: I'll post incident summary in #incidents and schedule a quick postmortem meeting 48h out. Please add any logs/traces to the incident thread.

maria-runtime: one more note — bisect job template: `rv deploy canary --variant v7.3.0-5d2b9c-off --nodes 5` then `rv deploy canary --variant v7.3.0-7a1f00-off --nodes 5` compare p95/p99 over 15m windows. We'll attach the exact metrics queries to the runbook.

raj-sre: saved traces: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/trace-req_3f7a (internal), dashboard snapshot: https://graphs.redwood.ai/d/latency/canary-2026-03-15.

support-alex: closing loop with customers: will send update that we mitigated and paused rollout; will follow up with postmortem once root cause fixed.

eli-oncall: thanks team — mitigation successful, moving to postmortem and bisect.
